subject: Account health: throughput spike, error-rate impact, and follow-through
messages:
From: Adam Shaw <adam.shaw@meridianretail.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sustained latency & errors impacting checkout - need executive liaison

Team,

We saw a second sustained spike this morning across our checkout routing: 99th percentile token latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s starting 08:30 PDT and error-rate (5xx) rose to ~2.7% for ~40 minutes. This caused timeouts on several cart attachments and a small but measurable drop in conversion.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood confirm root-cause hypothesis and ETA for mitigation?
- We need an exec-level owner for communications with our VP of Engineering.
- Please share any temporary workarounds (e.g., routing to fallback model variant) we can enable now.

Attaching a short screenshot of the latency graph and a link to our internal incident channel.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Shaw
Head of SRE, MeridianRetail
[Attachment: rps_latency_graph.png (image/png)]

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained latency & errors impacting checkout - need executive liaison

Adam — thanks for flagging and for the graph. We're on it. Quick notes and immediate actions: 

1) I'm spinning up an expedited bridge with infra & runtime leads (Laura & Neha included). Bridge details to follow in 5 min.
2) Short-term mitigation: we can route Meridian traffic to a smaller model shard with lower concurrency to reduce tail latency; that will reduce throughput by ~12% but should lower 99p latency. If you approve, we'll flip the routing policy now.
3) We're assigning Laura as primary on-engineer for follow-through and Kim (cc'd) as customer success liaison for exec comms.

Please confirm whether you want the routing fallback enabled while we investigate.

—David
David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, Adam Shaw <adam.shaw@meridianretail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained latency & errors impacting checkout - need executive liaison

Adam / team — bridge summary and immediate technical actions from infra/runtime: 

Bridge highlights (summary):
- Observed root pattern: a combination of an aggressive batching window increase rolled by the serving runtime last week and an external cache warmup failure for a subset of high-cardinality prefixes. The batching increase amplified KV misses which drove longer kernel times on the GPU at high concurrency.
- Immediate mitigation enacted (16:05 PDT): routing switch to the smaller-model variant + reduced max-concurrency cap for Meridian's service slice. Effect: 99p latency returned to ~310ms within 8 minutes; error-rate dropped to 0.14%.

Next steps (short horizon):
- Neha to run a deterministic replay of peak traffic with the new batching profile to validate no regression (ETA: 24 hours).
- Create a corrective actions tracker and map owners for each item (attachments below).
- Schedule executive readout Tue 08/17 11:00 PDT to walk the Meridian execs through root cause and remaining risk.

Attachments: corrective_actions_tracker.xlsx (working doc).

Laura Bennett
Sr. PM, Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Shaw <adam.shaw@meridianretail.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained latency & errors impacting checkout - need executive liaison

Quick technical note — preliminary RCA and items I'm tracking: 

Preliminary root cause (short):
- A config push to the batching controller increased the dynamic batching window by 35% for GPU-optimized kernels. Under Meridian's traffic shape (bursty short sequences), this increased intra-batch variance and amplified KV cache churn.
- A failure in our cache rehydration path for certain prefix hashes meant cache hit-rate dropped ~27% at peak. The combination increased GPU kernel time at tail and caused timeout cascades in upstream queuing.

Corrective items I'm actioning now (owner / ETA):
- Revert batching window change in prod for affected model families (owner: Neha) — ETA: 3 hours (in testing).
- Add a short-circuit to prefer cached prefix matches for high-priority customer slices (owner: Laura) — ETA: 48 hours.
- Post-incident eval: quantitative vuln test of recent runtime kernel changes (owner: Neha) — ETA: 72 hours.

I've updated the attached tracker with owners and initial status. Will surface test results to the bridge and the exec readout.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Lead SRE, Runtime Performance, Redwood Inference
